stem: A Massachusetts ambulatory care clinic has obtained approval from its medical staff executive committee for collaborative drug therapy management. The collaborating pharmacist works remotely from another site, reviewing records and speaking to patients by telephone. No physician is present with her. Is the arrangement compliant?

choices.text: Yes, because the correct approving body has approved the arrangement.
Yes, because the statute does not regulate where the pharmacist works.
Yes, provided the attending physician is reachable during clinic hours.
No, because the clinic setting requires on-site supervision by the attending physician.
No, because collaborative practice may not be conducted in an ambulatory care clinic.

explanation.core_reasoning: The ambulatory care clinic limb of the statute carries a condition none of the other listed settings does: collaborative practice there is permitted WITH ON-SITE SUPERVISION BY THE ATTENDING PHYSICIAN AND A COLLABORATING PHARMACIST, subject to approval by the clinic's medical staff executive committee or designee, or medical director or designee. Approval and on-site supervision are cumulative.

choice_analysis.A: Approval satisfies one condition; on-site supervision is another.
choice_analysis.B: The statute expressly attaches an on-site condition in this setting.
choice_analysis.C: Reachability is not the same as on-site supervision.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: on-site supervision is required in this setting.
choice_analysis.E: Ambulatory care clinics are an authorised setting.

related_facts: No other listed setting carries an on-site supervision condition
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates check the approval box and stop, because approval is the condition every setting shares.

reasoning_steps: Identify the setting as an ambulatory care clinic
Read the on-site supervision condition attached to it
Treat approval and supervision as cumulative
